subject: Order Form: cap scaling approach & exclusions — synthesis for legal
messages:
From: Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@brightwave.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form — Liability cap and carve-outs

Stephanie — attaching v3 of the order form with our in-line comments. Two asks from BrightWave legal: 1) uncapped liability for regulatory fines arising from personal data breaches; and 2) a higher cap tied to our annual spend rather than a flat number.

Quick summary of our position: we need an operational remedy for catastrophic privacy events; a multiple of annual fees (we proposed 2x annual spend) gives better alignment with potential downstream damage and is more acceptable to our board.

Attachments: BrightWave_Draft_OrderForm_v3.docx (annotated)

Happy to hop on a short call this week to go through the redlines.

— Ben
Head of Procurement, BrightWave Analytics
T: +1 415 555 0182

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@brightwave.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — Liability cap and carve-outs

Ben — thanks for the annotated draft and the clear summary. We reviewed with legal + finance this morning. High level response: we can be flexible on moving to an "annualized" construct, but we prefer a blended approach that balances predictability for both sides.

Proposed compromise (Redwood counter):
- Tiered cap: rolling 12-month cap = 150% of trailing 12-month paid fees (calculated monthly) to cover operational exposure;
- Hard contract maximum = $6,000,000 across the contract term (so very large tail events are still bounded);
- Exclusions: (a) liability for gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) IP infringement indemnity per usual; (c) regulatory fines remain excluded from liability cap but we are open to cooperation obligations and a carve-in for proven direct regulatory fines only where Redwood's control and negligence are established.

Rationale: the rolling 12-month formula tracks your spend profile and gives you a larger effective cap as usage grows, while the hard $6M backstop limits outsized exposure for Redwood. We think this is reasonable for enterprise customers with variable usage.

Can you confirm whether BrightWave would accept a limited carve-in for direct regulatory fines tied to Redwood's proven breach (i.e., where Redwood is found to have willfully or negligently caused the breach) rather than full uncapped exposure? That is the main sticking point for us.

If you want, we can prepare a marked-up Order Form that reflects the exact language and the computation example (monthly trailing calculation) and circulate to legal.

Thanks — happy to take this to a call if helpful.

— Stephanie
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | legal@redwood.com

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightwave.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@brightwave.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — Liability cap and carve-outs

Stephanie / team — quick response from BrightWave legal after internal review. Appreciate the creative proposal; our key priorities below: 

1) We cannot accept a hard $6M cap as the only backstop for our most sensitive datasets. Our board expects a carve-out for regulatory fines and statutory penalties related to personal data. We understand Redwood's concern about open-ended exposure, so here's a possible path: uncapped responsibility for regulatory fines only where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is proven (narrow standard), and for other breaches a higher rolling cap (BrightWave's ask is 200% of trailing 12 months).

2) We want to preserve consequential damages carve-out for both sides but keep explicit language protecting customer loss of revenue caused by a service outage originating from Redwood's infrastructure (operational SLA failures). That would be limited and subject to caps/step-downs.

3) Please include an illustrative calculation for a 12-month trailing example in the Order Form so the commercial team can approve quickly.

We can accept a call Thursday morning PT to finalize.

— Sara
Senior Counsel, BrightWave Analytics
Attachments: none

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@brightwave.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@brightwave.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2028 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — Liability cap and carve-outs

Thanks all — good progress. Next steps from Redwood side (action items):

1) Internal legal redline: we'll generate a marked-up Order Form that implements the tiered approach (150% rolling 12-month + $6M hard cap) and add a narrowly-tailored carve-in for regulatory fines tied to proven gross negligence or willful misconduct. We'll also draft an SLA-linked limited consequential damages remedy (formula + step-downs) for operational outages. Expect that redline by EOD Monday. Attachment: Redwood_Cap_Table_Scenarios.xlsx (shows 3 usage profiles with numerical examples).

2) Commercial alignment: Markus / Laura to confirm whether the $6M hard cap is acceptable commercially given typical enterprise ARRs; if not, we'll propose escalation paths (finance-backed letters or excess-liability insurance options).

3) Call: We'll hold the Thursday 09:30 PT call per Sara's availability to go over the marked-up language and calculation example. Calendar invite to follow.

Please confirm if BrightWave wants a separate clause on regulatory cooperation (forensics, notifications, regulatory defense cooperation) — we will include standard cooperation covenants.

Best — Stephanie
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: Redwood_Cap_Table_Scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet with scenario outputs)
